newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices hit new record highs.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices hit new record highs.

text.p: Danish bond prices, buoyed by foreign market gains and well-received U.S. producer prices, reached new heights on Friday and looked headed for more gains next week, but a dealer said that a downturn lay ahead.
"Even though everything points toward a strong market next week too, a correction has got to come before long," he said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 closed at 112.81, yielding 6.11 percent, up from Thursday's 112.30 and surpassing the previous 12-month closing high of 112.50.
Turnover in the benchmark was 2.7 billion crowns. Its March future rose 0.14 point to 111.96, with 35 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.35 point to 90.20.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed to 62 basis points from 64 bp.
The crown stood at 3.8115 to the mark, firming from Thursday's 3.8120.
The central bank took advantage of the rising market to sell close to a billion crowns worth of mainly longer-dated paper, a player said. --Soeren Linding Jakobsen, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969651
